issues.legal_issue: A delayed application to substitute the legal representatives of deceased respondents in a certified appeal may be allowed when sufficient cause for the delay is shown and the applicable time-extension power is exercised.
material_facts: The appeal was pending after a certificate had been granted and before the record was dispatched to the Supreme Court.
Two respondents died during that period, and applications to substitute their legal representatives were filed more than 90 days after their deaths.
The Court found sufficient cause for condoning the delay and considered that it could also enlarge the prescribed time.
issues.conclusion: The Court enlarged the time for filing the applications and directed that the legal representatives of the deceased respondents be substituted.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XVI Rule 12 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1950, an application to substitute a deceased party before dispatch of the record was subject to a 90-day period, but delay could be condoned under Section 5 of the Limitation Act; Order XLV Rule 3 of the Supreme Court Rules also empowered the Court to enlarge a time fixed by those Rules.

predicates.certified_appeal_pending_before_record_d: A certified appeal was pending before the record was dispatched to the Supreme Court.
predicates.respondents_died_during_proceedings: One or more respondents died while the appeal proceedings were pending.
predicates.substitution_applications_filed_after_de: Applications to substitute the deceased respondents' legal representatives were filed after the prescribed filing period.
predicates.sufficient_cause_for_delay: The Court found sufficient cause for the delay in applying to substitute the deceased respondents' legal representatives.
predicates.time_for_respondent_substitution_extende: The time for applying to substitute the deceased respondents' legal representatives is extended.

issues.definition: When respondents die during a certified appeal pending before record dispatch, applications are late, and sufficient cause for delay is shown, the time for respondent substitution is extended.

issues.legal_issue: The time for an application to substitute a deceased appellant in a pending appeal may be enlarged even when the applicable procedural rule does not expressly provide for condoning delay.
material_facts: An appellant died after the appeal records had been dispatched to the Supreme Court but before a formal petition of appeal was lodged there.
The application to substitute the appellant's legal representative was filed more than 90 days after the death.
The Court found that its power to enlarge time applied and, in the circumstances, granted an extension.
issues.conclusion: The Court enlarged the time for filing the substitution application and directed that the deceased appellant's legal representative be substituted.
issues.legal_principle: Order XVI Rules 13 and 14 of the Supreme Court Rules, 1950 required an application to substitute a deceased appellant to be filed within 90 days, and Order XVI Rule 14A made the abatement provisions of Order XXII of the Code of Civil Procedure applicable. Although the relevant rule did not provide for condonation under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, Order XLV Rule 13 of the Supreme Court Rules empowered the Court to enlarge the time fixed by the Rules.

rule.if: appeal_pending_before_formal_filing and appellant_died_during_proceedings and substitution_application_filed_after_deadline and case_circumstances_support_extension

predicates.appeal_pending_before_formal_filing: An appeal was pending before its formal filing in the Supreme Court.
predicates.appellant_died_during_proceedings: An appellant died while the appeal proceedings were pending.
predicates.substitution_application_filed_after_dea: The application to substitute the deceased appellant's legal representative was filed after the prescribed filing period.
predicates.case_circumstances_support_extension: The circumstances of the case supported enlarging the time for the substitution application.
predicates.time_for_appellant_substitution_extended: The time for applying to substitute the deceased appellant's legal representative is extended.

issues.definition: When an appellant dies while an appeal is pending before formal filing, the substitution application is late, and the circumstances support an extension, the time for appellant substitution is extended.

issues.legal_issue: A final decree cannot be made against parties to a partition suit who were not bound by a preliminary decree.
material_facts: The trial court dismissed the partition suit in its entirety.
On appeal, only some defendants entered into a compromise with the plaintiffs.
The appellate court disposed of the appeal in terms of that compromise without passing a preliminary decree against the defendants who did not join it.
A final decree was later made against those nonjoining defendants following proceedings to prepare the partition.
issues.conclusion: The final-decree proceedings were invalid as against the defendants who had not joined the compromise, because no preliminary decree had been passed against them; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A compromise decree does not bind parties who did not join the compromise, and a final decree cannot be made against a party unless a preliminary decree has first been passed against that party. The Court relied on no earlier cases for this principle.

predicates.partition_suit_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal arising from a partition suit.
predicates.compromise_involves_only_some_parties: Only some of the parties to the suit entered into the compromise on which the appellate disposition was based.
predicates.no_preliminary_decree_against_nonjoining: No preliminary decree determining the rights of the parties who did not join the compromise was passed.
predicates.final_decree_sought_against_nonjoining_p: A final decree was pursued against parties who did not join the compromise.
predicates.final_decree_unavailable_against_nonjoin: A final decree cannot be made against parties who were not bound by a preliminary decree.

issues.definition: When a partition-suit appeal is resolved by a compromise involving only some parties, no preliminary decree is passed against the nonjoining parties, and a final decree is pursued against them, that final decree is unavailable against those parties.
